competences: The learner identifies key facts about government revenue.
The learner explains information about Taxation and types of taxes using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes taxes, taxation, tax, revenue.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about government revenue.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Taxation and types of taxes.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about government revenue.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Taxation and types of taxes
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces government revenue. They ask "Which group of people paid the following taxes?" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about government revenue
steps.content: Taxation/ taxes Taxes Lack of information about the taxes to be paid. They started paying taxes It is charged as value added to a commodity. Why people should pay taxes. Government raises money to provide social services. Why some people do not pay taxes. Taxes are too high. People dodge paying taxes Taxation is the system of collecting money as taxes Taxes Indirect tax This is the type of tax paid on goods and services indirectly.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about government revenue on the chalkboard, including "Taxation/ taxes Taxes; Lack of information about the taxes to be paid.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about government revenue
steps.content: This is the tax paid directly by the people This is the body responsible for collecting and assessing taxes on behalf of the government . To assess taxes. steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about government revenue on the chalkboard, including "This is the tax paid directly by the people; This is the body responsible for collecting and assessing taxes on behalf of the government .". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about government revenue
steps.content: Hut tax - hut owners Gun tax – gun owners The main source of government revenue in Uganda is taxes/ tax collection TRADE Indirect tax Direct tax This is tax collected directly from the person who pays it URA is the body in charge of collecting taxes in Uganda Indirect tax. This is tax paid on imports/ goods entering a country.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about government revenue on the chalkboard, including "Hut tax - hut owners; Gun tax – gun owners". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: Which group of people paid the following taxes? | How did the 1900 Buganda agreement affect the following? | How were local people able to pay taxes? | Why did the British make local people to pay taxes? | Mention the two types of taxes.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Which group of people paid the following taxes?" and "How did the 1900 Buganda agreement affect the following?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on government revenue, asks "Which group of people paid the following taxes?" and follows up with "How did the 1900 Buganda agreement affect the following?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Which group of people paid the following taxes?" and "How did the 1900 Buganda agreement affect the following?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Name the body that is responsible for collecting taxes in Uganda."
